newsitem.title: USA: Forty-two House Democrats protest EPA air proposal.
newsitem.headline: Forty-two House Democrats protest EPA air proposal.

text.p: A group of Democratic congressmen asked to meet with President Bill Clinton to protest the administration's proposed air quality standards that they said would unfairly penalise large cities, Representative John Dingell said on Tuesday.

In a letter to the president made public Tuesday, a total of 42 House Democrats, many from the industrial Ohio Valley and upper Midwestern areas, criticised the Environmental Protection Agency's proposed new air quality standards for ozone, or smog, and particulate matter, or soot.

The proposed changes would transform more than 400 U.S. counties into areas that do not meet the new standards even though actual air quality in the counties has been steadily improving, the letter said.

"These counties, which include the vast majority of the nation's urban and suburban areas, will face an indefinite future of growth restrictions and potential disruption of highway funding and other sanctions," the congressmen told the president.

The EPA's proposals "raise difficult issues that should be carefully considered before the administration makes its final decisions," said the letter dated April 24. It said the EPA should consider alternatives that may do as much or more to improve air quality.
The EPA is to announce a final decision in July on its proposal to sharply tighten the standards which the agency said may be necessary to protect public health.
Smokestack industries and a number of state and local government officials say meeting the new standards would cost billions of dollars while providing minimal health gains.
Dingell, ranking Commerce Committee Democrat, said the planned EPA changes would disrupt efforts now under way for cleaner air, and would restrict economic growth.
